children.approach: Lemma: the Hessian of d^beta N(h) has entries M_ij = c_{beta+e_i+e_j}, the RAW coefficients, since d^gamma((c_gamma/gamma!)x^gamma) = c_gamma. Consequence: the 2x2-minor necessary condition (RLC) is log-concavity of the RAW coefficients, and the same inequality on normalized coefficients is strictly weaker (factorial ratio alpha_i alpha_j / ((alpha_i+1)(alpha_j+1)) < 1). Verified symbolically over all beta at ell=3, d=4.

Theorem: if c_gamma = prod_t f_t(gamma_t) with each f_t log-concave with interval support (PF_2), then N(h) is Lorentzian. Mechanism: M = P uu^T - (nonneg diagonal), so lambda_2 <= lambda_2(rank-one PSD) = 0 by Weyl; the four cases |Z|=0,1,2,>=3 of zero-indices Z={k: f_k(beta_k)=0} are handled separately (|Z|=1 gives an arrow matrix of rank <=2 with negative 2x2 determinant). (L2) proved directly by the box-slice exchange axiom. Controls: 1105 random product-form instances, 0 failures; NEGATIVE control, 3604 of 5573 non-log-concave product forms FAIL (L3), so the hypothesis is load-bearing.

Corollary: for m=1 the cylindric horizontal-strip condition reads nu_1 <= rho_1 < nu_1 + n, so K^c_alpha = prod_t 1_{[0,n-1]}(alpha_t) exactly; 1_{[0,n-1]} is PF_2, so product-form applies. Settles every one-bead cylindric shape at every level n and every ell. Contains a two-line proof that e_d is Lorentzian (n=2: M = J_S - I_S, lambda_2 = -1). Characterisation checked against the chain recursion: 165/165 for 2<=n<=7, d<=n, ell<=5. The family WINDS, so this is not a restatement of the ordinary case.

Proposition: at ell=2 the constraints on the single intermediate cylindric shape kappa DECOUPLE -- kappa_i in [max(mu_i, lam_{i-1}+1), min(lam_i, mu_{i+1}-1)], one independent interval per bead, each involving only the fixed data mu,lam. The tuple is automatically a cylindric shape (kappa_i <= mu_{i+1}-1 < mu_{i+1} <= kappa_{i+1}; wrap from mu_{m+1}=mu_1+n). Hence sum_a k_a z^a is a product of interval indicators. Checked against BOTH the chain recursion and brute-force enumeration of intermediate shapes: 3224/3224 shapes for 2<=n<=7, 1<=m<=n, d<=10.

Lemma (classically Hoggar, but proved here from scratch so as not to rest on an uncited source): PF_2 = log-concave with interval support is closed under convolution. Proof: T(f*g) = T(f)T(g) on bi-infinite Toeplitz matrices, and by Cauchy-Binet every 2x2 minor of a product is a finite sum of products of pairs of 2x2 minors; nonnegativity of all 2x2 Toeplitz minors is verified directly for an interval indicator (the anti-diagonal index pair {r,s} is strictly more spread than {p,q} at equal sum, so f(r)f(s)=1 forces f(p)f(q)=1) and implies log-concavity (rows {i,i+1}, cols {k,k+1}). Controls: 3e5 random interval-indicator minors, 0 negative; 44409 random PF_2 convolution pairs, 0 failures.

Theorem: N(s^c_{lambda/mu}(x_1,x_2)) is Lorentzian for EVERY cylindric skew shape, every level n, every m. From ell2-decoupling + pf2-convolution the sequence k_a = K^c_{(a,d-a)} is log-concave with interval support; (L2) is then the interval property and (L3) is det[[k_{a+2},k_{a+1}],[k_{a+1},k_a]] = k_a k_{a+2} - k_{a+1}^2 <= 0 via raw-hessian-lemma.

Q256 falsifier, run BEFORE attempting the proof as the brief required. 3647 instances (2<=n<=6, 1<=m<=n, d<=9, 2<=ell<=6), 1899 winding (52.1%): ZERO failures of (L2), of exact (L3), or of (RLC) on raw coefficients. A 517-instance subsweep (228 winding, 44.1%) also found 0 failures of the normalized (RLC). All (L3) decisions exact: integer characteristic polynomial by Faddeev-LeVerrier over Q plus Descartes' rule (exact for real-rooted polynomials), never float eigenvalues. Instrument controls: HMMS Thm 3 positive control 16/16; three planted negative controls all refused; the exact eigenvalue counter was WRONG on first writing (mis-indexed Faddeev-LeVerrier) and after correction agrees with numpy on 4000/4000 random integer symmetric matrices.

Census of where (L3) is tight, to constrain any future proof. Among the 2238 nonzero Hessians from WINDING instances with m>=2: lambda_2 = 0 EXACTLY in 1637 (73.1%), lambda_2 < 0 in 601 (26.9%). So the conjecture, if true, sits on the boundary of the Lorentzian cone about three times in four -- no argument with slack can work. Separately, the product-form mechanism (off-diagonal part of M rank one, i.e. M_ij M_kl = M_il M_kj for distinct i,j,k,l) holds in 1280/1658 Hessians with ell>=4 (77.2%) and fails in 22.8%.

This is the natural form of the exchange route, because sign-reversing involutions produce exactly pairwise exchange inequalities.

children.approach: ATTEMPT: reduce to the ordinary case via Postnikov's toric Schur theorem, which in its range of validity expands s^c in Schur functions with nonnegative Gromov-Witten coefficients, then apply HMMS Thm 3 (normalized Schur polynomials are Lorentzian).
children.reason: Shut on BOTH sides, and the second reason is the serious one because it survives where positivity holds. (a) Outside Postnikov's range the Schur coefficients of s^c can be NEGATIVE -- smallest instance n=3, m=1, lam=(3), ell=3, where s^c = s_{21} - s_{111} (13 winding instances found 2026-09-25). (b) Even inside the positive range the reduction is invalid, because the Lorentzian polynomials of a fixed degree are NOT closed under addition: (x+y)^2 and (2x+y)^2 are each Lorentzian (rank-one PSD Hessian, lambda_2 = 0) but their sum 5x^2+6xy+2y^2 has Hessian [[10,6],[6,4]], det 4 > 0, trace 14 > 0, two positive eigenvalues (13.7082, 0.2918). A sum of two rank-one PSD forms with independent kernels has rank two.

children.approach: THE OPEN REGIME, stated precisely: ell >= 3 AND m >= 2. The reason the ell=2 proof does not generalise is structural, not technical: the horizontal-strip condition kappa^{t+1}_i < kappa^t_{i+1} makes bead i at time t+1 depend on bead i+1 at time t, so consecutive INTERIOR layers couple and the coefficient sequence stops being a convolution of independent interval indicators. The coupling is absent at ell=2 because there is only one interior layer, and absent at m=1 because i+1 = i. Any future certificate must (a) see >= 3 indices at once (rlc-implies-l3), (b) be exact rather than slack (tightness-census: 73.1% of winding m>=2 Hessians have lambda_2 = 0 exactly), and (c) supply a combinatorial formula for the rank-one part -- NOTE that such a decomposition always EXISTS whenever lambda_2 <= 0 (take lambda_1 p p^T minus the rest), so the 22.8% figure in tightness-census bounds the reach of THAT certificate, and is not evidence that no certificate exists. || 2026-09-29 c1: reduced to exactly two combinatorial inequalities (conj-A-logconcave, conj-B-logsubmodular) via metric-criterion + l3-det-reduction; gap localised to a cancellation across an antichain (order-by-S-kappa).

Corollary: condition (B) holds at ell=3, every level n, whenever the admissible inner shapes kappa form a CHAIN under containment - in particular for m=1. Proof: if the chain is graded by S_kappa then for u<u' every kappa in the fibre {S_kappa=u} is <= every kappa' in {S_kappa=u'}, and summing a TP2 matrix over CONSECUTIVE blocks of rows preserves TP2 because each 2x2 minor of the blocked matrix is a sum of 2x2 minors of the original with rows drawn from the earlier and later block. Then comparable-mlr gives P(u,.) <=_lr P(u',.), which is (B).

Lemma 1: a symmetric 3x3 M with nonnegative entries satisfying (A) M_ij^2>=M_ii M_jj and (B) M_ik M_kj >= M_ij M_kk has at most one positive eigenvalue. Proof: the identity det M = P+2t-x-y-z with xyz=P t^2 (P=prod diag, t=prod offdiag, x=M_11 M_23^2 etc); (B) multiplied through gives exactly x,y,z <= t, so for t>0 det M = t*g(x/t,y/t,z/t) with g(xi,eta,zeta)=xi*eta*zeta-xi-eta-zeta+2 MULTILINEAR, hence minimised at a vertex of [0,1]^3 where it takes values 2,1,0,0. (A) gives e_2(M)<=0 separately. e_2<=0 and det>=0 forbid two positive eigenvalues. Equality det M=0 iff at least two of the three (B) consequences are tight - matches 3921/3921 Hessians. Equivalent phrasing: (A)+(B) say log(M_ij/sqrt(M_ii M_jj)) is a pseudometric. Adversarial search: 45301 integer matrices satisfying (A)&(B), 0 with det<0, 0 with >1 positive eigenvalue; negative controls bite (A alone 21135/54068, B alone 526/23089). Uses NOTHING from Branden-Huh.
extend Lemma 1 from 3x3 to general ell, which combined with (A),(B) verified at ell=4,5,6 would give a criterion for every ell

The STRUCTURAL witness is at ell=5: normalising N_ij=M_ij/sqrt(M_ii M_jj)=exp(phi_ij), conditions (A)+(B) say phi is a pseudometric, and on {sum x_i = 0} one gets x'Nx = sum_{i!=j}(exp(phi_ij)-1) x_i x_j, so the criterion needs (exp(phi)-1) to be conditionally negative definite ('of negative type'). Not every metric is of negative type; the K_{2,3} shortest-path metric (phi=1 across the parts, 2 within) gives N with spectrum {-6.389,-6.389,-6.389,+4.469,+19.698} - TWO positive eigenvalues - while satisfying (A) and (B) exactly. SCOPE OF THIS REASON: it refutes the CRITERION for ell>=4, NOT (L3) itself at ell>=4; the cylindric pseudometrics may well all be of negative type, and (A),(B) were verified without exception on 143375 Hessians at ell=4,5,6. This is precisely why ell=3 is the right target and the choice is now explained rather than assumed.

children.approach: Proposition: for a symmetric 3x3 M with nonnegative entries (so tr M >= 0), M has at most one positive eigenvalue IFF e_2(M)<=0 AND det M>=0. Forward: lambda_1>=0>=lambda_2>=lambda_3 gives det>=0, and tr>=0 gives lambda_1 >= -(lambda_2+lambda_3), whence e_2 <= -(lambda_2^2+lambda_2 lambda_3+lambda_3^2)<=0. Converse: lambda_2>0 with det>=0 forces lambda_3>=0 hence e_2>=lambda_1 lambda_2>0. CONSEQUENCE: since e_2(M) is exactly the SUM of the three raw RLC quantities, and RLC has never failed in this programme, the entire open content of (L3) at ell=3 is the single inequality det M >= 0. This is also why rlc-implies-l3 died: its witness has all three 2x2 minors <=0 but det=-16.

Proposition: at ell=3, K^c_{(a,b,c)} counts pairs (kappa,sigma) in Z^m x Z^m with mu_i <= kappa_i <= mu_{i+1}-1, lam_{i-1}+1 <= sigma_i <= lam_i, and kappa_i <= sigma_i <= kappa_{i+1}-1 (cyclically, x_{i+m}=x_i+n), graded by a=S_kappa-|mu|, b=S_sigma-S_kappa, c=|lam|-S_sigma. Proof is a direct unfolding of the horizontal-strip condition nu_i <= rho_i < nu_{i+1}; no separate shape check is needed since kappa_i <= mu_{i+1}-1 < mu_{i+1} <= kappa_{i+1}. Verified against the independent transfer-matrix DP on 911/911 instances, 0 disagreements. Consequence: the solution set is cut out by difference constraints x_p - x_q <= c alone, hence is a SUBLATTICE of Z^{2m}, and (S_kappa,S_sigma) is linear hence modular on it.

Lemma 2: if f <=_lr f', g <=_lr g' and all four are PF2, then f*g <=_lr f'*g'. Proof: reduce by transitivity to one factor at a time; then for v<v', S := (f*g)(v)(f'*g)(v') - (f*g)(v')(f'*g)(v) = sum_{w,w'} f(w)f'(w') Delta(w,w') with Delta antisymmetric, so 2S = sum [f(w)f'(w')-f(w')f'(w)] Delta(w,w'); the first bracket is >=0 for w<w' by f<=_lr f', and Delta(w,w') = g(p)g(p'+delta)-g(p+delta)g(p') >= 0 for p>p' by PF2 of g. Both brackets are antisymmetric and sign-matched, so every term is >=0. Tested on 97289 random PF2 TP2 quadruples with 0 failures; negative control dropping PF2 fails 99/484, so the PF2 hypothesis is load-bearing. Distinct from the existing pf2-convolution node, which says PF2 is closed under convolution; this says the LIKELIHOOD RATIO ORDER between two convolutions is preserved.

Lemma 3: with W_kappa = conv_i 1_{[L_i(kappa),R_i(kappa)]}, L_i=max(kappa_i,lam_{i-1}+1), R_i=min(kappa_{i+1}-1,lam_i), if kappa <= kappa' coordinatewise then W_kappa <=_lr W_kappa'. Proof: L_i and R_i are each nondecreasing in kappa, two interval indicators with both endpoints weakly increasing form a TP2 pair (direct check), interval indicators are PF2, and lr-convolution applies inductively over the m beads. Verified on 15147 comparable pairs, 0 failures.
